conviction_note: Q3 consensus ($204.1M) sits exactly on the midpoint of the company's own -8% to -10% guide ($202.0-206.5M on Q3 2025's $224.5M), INSP beat revenue in each of the last four quarters, management called prior-auth submissions an improving leading indicator and said it was cautious about narrowing a wide FY range, and 15.9% of float is short with the stock down 6.8% in five days; against that the stock has re-rated ~30% since the pre-Q2 $50 and trades at or above most targets, and this name trades on guidance, not on the quarter (moves of -32, +15, -12.6, -12, +22.8 all followed the guide). So a mild up lean, p_up 55, on a scale at the 14.2% implied move; the findings sum (+1.8) and the scaled number (+1.45) agree in sign and size.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar is the company's own guide midpoint: consensus $204.1M (Benzinga, Earnings Whispers) equals the midpoint of the -8% to -10% y/y guide ($202.0-206.5M on $224.5M), INSP has beaten revenue consensus in each of the last four quarters by 0.65%-3.02% (Benzinga), and on the Q2 call management said prior-authorization submissions (its stated leading indicator) were improving, the coding/WISeR hit would 'decrease sequentially' in Q3 and Q4, and most of the top-25% centers would be educated on -52 modifier billing during Q3; a ~1-3% revenue beat ($206-210M) is the base case, landing at or just above the top of the guided range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats have not paid on their own here: Q4 2025 beat and the stock fell (-12.55% on 2026-02-11, with a cut 2026 outlook); Q3 2025 beat ($224.5M vs $220.2M est.) and rose +15.33% alongside an EPS raise; Q2 2026 revenue $200.6M beat with a FY raise and rose +22.83%. The quarter alone has been secondary to the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: A beat inside or just above the guided range is largely expected (consensus sits on the midpoint, so a top-of-range print is a ~1% beat); if the market expected a large beat, consensus would sit above the midpoint and the stock would not have given back 6.8% in the last five sessions.
findings.independence: Beat history from Benzinga earnings page (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/INSP/earnings-forecasts); Q3 2025 base from the company 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1609550/000160955025000052/insp2025-q3pressreleaseex9.htm). Shares the Q2-call transcript with the guidance finding below.

findings.finding: Management left a wide FY2026 revenue range ($835-875M, $40M wide with one quarter left after Q3) and the CFO said explicitly 'we just want to be cautious about narrowing the range', with H2 assumed 'only slightly better' than Q2 and the FY coding/WISeR hit at $120-130M; the single FY consensus figure found ($848.9M, MarketBeat) sits $6M below the $855M midpoint, so a Q3 at or above the top of its guide makes a narrowing toward the upper half, or a raised low end, the likely guidance action on this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This stock trades on the guide: 2025-08-04 guidance cut -32.35%; 2026-02-11 2026 outlook cut below expectations -12.55%; 2026-05-04 outlook cut -12.02%; 2026-08-03 outlook raised (rev low end +$10M, adj EPS +$0.30 at midpoint) +22.83%. Each guide direction produced a double-digit move.
findings.why_not_priced: The narrowing is an inference from the CFO's stated caution and the sequential-improvement assumptions, not a disclosed number; the FY consensus below the guide midpoint and the 6.8% five-day decline show the market is not leaning on a raise. If a raise were priced, the stock would have held its October ~$70.6-70.8 level into the print and FY consensus would sit above $855M.
findings.independence: FY guide figures from the 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001609550/000160955026000045/insp2026-q2pressreleaseex9.htm); FY consensus $848.9M from MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/inspire-medical-systems-nyseinsp-updates-fy-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-03/), a single source, so capped. Shares the transcript with the reported-quarter finding.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-02 Inspire announced the AMA CPT Editorial Panel approved new Category I HGNS codes covering single-lead implants including Inspire V (effective 2028-01-01, CMS proposed valuations July 2027, final November 2027), backed by AAO-HNS, AASM and ISSS; this removes the main structural coding question for 2028 and gives management a firmer base for any 2027/2028 framing on the call, but the stock moved about +2% around it and the code does not affect 2026-27 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Coding news has been the dominant driver this year (2026 code change behind the Q4/Q1 guide cuts); the approval itself drew ~+2% (close $70.78 on 2026-10-01, the prior session per RTTNews).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public company announcement a month ago. What is not priced is how management uses it on the call to frame 2027-28; if the market had priced a confident 2027 return-to-growth framing, the stock would not have drifted back from ~$70.8 to $66.2.
findings.independence: Q2 call said the revised application was going to the September panel with a 2028-01-01 target (https://www.webull.com/news/15381724343198720).

findings.finding: Competitor Nyxoah pre-announced Q3 on 2026-10-19: US net revenue ~EUR6.7M (+29% q/q), global ~EUR9.2M, FY2026 revenue guide cut to EUR33-35M from EUR36-40M, citing a ramp 'more reflective of historical ramps for a new technology'; patients under prior authorization entering Q4 were 447 against 427 entering Q3 (+5%) after +77% the quarter before. Read-through cuts both ways: the only US HGNS competitor is ramping slower than it guided (positive for INSP share, ~$7.8M vs INSP's ~$190M US quarter), while its flat prior-auth pipeline could hint at continued payer friction in the shared HGNS market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed INSP reaction to Nyxoah releases; Q2 call said competitor trials had no significant impact.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 6-K two weeks ago; the INSP read-through is ambiguous and small relative to INSP's scale, so it is filed at zero rather than left out.
findings.independence: Nyxoah Q2 figure of 427 patients under PA entering Q3 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nyxoah-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-05/) gives the comparison; Nyxoah attributes the cut to its own ramp, not market conditions.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 7.07% to 4.49M shares, 15.89% of float and 4.5 days to cover (record date 2026-10-15), and the stock fell 6.77% in the five sessions into the print with skew balanced (-1.63 vol points); on a name whose last guide raise produced +22.83%, a crowded and building short into an amc print with a likely in-range-or-better quarter adds squeeze asymmetry to any upside guidance outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-03: FY raise with short interest ~13.6-21% of float -> +22.83%; 2025-11-03 beat -> +15.33%. Downside reactions (-12 to -32%) happened on guide cuts regardless of positioning.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own bet, not a fact it is missing; what it adds is the reaction shape. If shorts expected an upside guide they would be covering, not building 7% into the print, and calls would carry a clear premium rather than the near-flat skew.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline run_up_5d -6.77% and skew -1.63 (baselines/INSP.json); a second data page on 2026-10-26 showed 4.6 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/insp).

findings.finding: ResMed's fiscal Q1 2027 (quarter to 2026-09-30, released 2026-10-30) showed revenue +6% (+7% constant currency) and management continued to frame GLP-1s as a tailwind to OSA patient flow (earlier data: GLP-1 patients ~10.7 points more likely to start PAP), a broad series that argues against a GLP-1 demand collapse in sleep apnea; INSP itself said GLP-1s don't 'really change our overall demand'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: INSP's moves this year have been on coding and reimbursement, not GLP-1 read-throughs.
findings.why_not_priced: Public three days ago and a macro-to-company proxy; filed small because INSP's demand question this year is reimbursement, not diagnosis flow.
findings.independence: Proxy; ResMed GLP-1 propensity data from earlier calls (https://hmenews.com/article/resmed-primes-patient-pump); INSP's own Q2 GLP-1 comment from the transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15381724343198720).

findings.finding: Expectations are no longer depressed the way they were at Q2: the stock was ~$50.21 going into the August print with a $51.53 mean target (Barchart), and at $66.21 it now trades above most published targets (Google Finance 3-month range $39-65, avg $52.27; Stockanalysis avg $60.4; JPMorgan Neutral $60 on 2026-08-04), with Q3 still guided to a y/y decline and management declining to guide 2027; the easy-bar setup that produced +22.83% has partly been used up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the +15.33% Q3 2025 move the stock ran to a $147 high and then fell -4.61%/-12.55%/-12.02% on the next three releases; re-rated names here have been sold on in-line guides.

outside_window.finding: New Category I CPT codes for single-lead HGNS take effect 2028-01-01, with CMS proposed valuations in July 2027 and final in November 2027; the 2028 rate is the real economic resolution of the coding issue.
